title: Va'era: the finger of God (Exodus 8:15)
hook: Pharaoh's magicians admit "This is the finger of God"

segments.voice: Yesterday, Va'era: Aaron struck the river, because it once saved Moses. Gratitude even to water. Today, the third plague, and the day the experts give up.

There's a moment every expert dreads. The mechanic who's seen every engine looks under the hood and goes quiet. The doctor says, honestly, I don't know. It takes a certain courage to say that out loud, especially if your job is to always have an answer. Pharaoh has a team of those experts: his court magicians. When Aaron turned the Nile to blood, they did the same trick. When frogs came up out of the river, they made frogs too. So far, they've matched every move. Then comes something tiny.
screen: `THE EXPERT GOES QUIET.` → `THE MAGICIANS MATCH EVERY MOVE.` → `THEN, SOMETHING TINY.`

segments.voice: Aaron strikes the dust of the earth, and it becomes lice, or gnats, the Hebrew word is uncertain, crawling on people and animals all over Egypt. The magicians try their arts to do the same, and they can't. So they go to Pharaoh and say, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "This is the finger of God." In Hebrew, etzba Elohim. Here's the surprise. Moses and Aaron have said all along that God sent them. But the first voices in Pharaoh's own court to admit it are his magicians, the professionals whose job was to explain everything away. And it's something small that does it, not something grand. The Talmud even notes that such magic can't produce anything smaller than a grain of barley; the tiniest thing is where their power runs out. Then the verse goes on: Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he wouldn't listen to them. The experts admitted it. The king refused. The phrase stuck around. In the Passover Haggadah, Rabbi Yose the Galilean does some playful math with it. If in Egypt it took only a finger to bring ten plagues, then at the sea, where the Torah speaks of God's great hand, five fingers, there must have been fifty. Families read that at the seder table every year. But the heart of the moment is the admission: three Hebrew words, etzba Elohim hi, from people with every reason not to say them. What they meant was: this is beyond us.
screen: `DUST BECOMES LICE.` · `THE MAGICIANS CAN'T DO IT.` · `ETZBA ELOHIM — THE FINGER OF GOD.` · `A FINGER IN EGYPT, A HAND AT THE SEA.` · then, large: `THE FINGER OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Think of one thing you've been pretending to have handled: a question at work you can't actually answer, a problem at home you can't fix alone, a worry that's bigger than you. Say it silently and plainly, this is beyond me, and notice how that feels in your body; maybe lighter. Then think of who you could say it to.
Va'era. The portion where Pharaoh's magicians, beaten by the smallest plague, admit: this is the finger of God.
Your line: the finger of God. Three small words, from the least likely mouths. Two hundred twenty-nine days now.

howItsDone: At the Passover seder, families read Rabbi Yose the Galilean's teaching in the Haggadah, counting ten plagues in Egypt by God's finger and fifty at the sea by God's hand.

fork.setup: you're one of Pharaoh's magicians. you've matched every plague so far. this time, you can't. what do you tell the king?
options: this is the finger of God.
fork.reveal: the magicians told Pharaoh: this is the finger of God. and Pharaoh's heart was hardened anyway.

original.note: Hebrew: the finger of God. The magicians' words to Pharaoh (Exodus 8:15).

trapdoor: what you thought: a dramatic line in a movie.
what it means: Pharaoh's own experts admit something is beyond them, and the king refuses to listen.
what a scholar hears: the verse is 8:15 in Hebrew Bibles and 8:19 in most English ones, and the Haggadah builds its plague arithmetic on it.

sources.quoted: This is the finger of God

notes: Confirm JPS 1917 wording 'This is the finger of God' (Exodus 8:15).
The Hebrew kinim is variously rendered lice or gnats; confirm the script's hedge.
Sanhedrin 67b (sorcery cannot create anything smaller than a barley grain; Rashi on 8:14 cites it) from memory; confirm.
Rabbi Yose the Galilean's ten and fifty plagues paraphrased from the Haggadah; confirm.

Audit (second sample): the teach said 'four small words' (the Hebrew is three, etzba Elohim hi; the English is five) and claimed the magicians were the first in the Exodus story to name God's hand, though Moses and Aaron had already spoken in God's name; both corrected.
